* US Troops are preventing a [[Red Crescent]] aid convoy from entering the city of [[Falluja]], reportedly for safety reasons [https://web.archive.org/web/20041122235209/http://www.reuters.co.uk/newsPackageArticle.jhtml?type=worldNews (Reuters)]
* [[Conflict in Iraq]]: Hundreds of [[US Troops]] are diverted from [[Falluja]] as insurgents [[Battle of Mosul (2004)|appear to take control]] of the northeastern city of [[Mosul]]. [http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/world/middle_east/4010549.stm (BBC)]
* [[Iran]] is reportedly concluding a deal with the [[European Union]] which would spare it from possible [[United Nations]] sanctions over its [[Iran's nuclear program|nuclear arms programme]]. [https://web.archive.org/web/20041122235209/http://www.reuters.co.uk/newsPackageArticle.jhtml?type=worldNews (Reuters)]
* [[United States Secretary of Education]] [[Rodney Paige|Rod Paige]] announces his intent to resign from his post, making him the third member of President [[George W. Bush]]'s Cabinet to resign since his re-election. No time-table has been set for his actually leaving the post. [[White House]] domestic policy adviser [[Margaret Spellings]] has been suggested as his successor. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/articles/A46017-2004Nov12.html (Washington Post)]  [https://www.reuters.com/newsArticle.jhtml?type=topNews&storyID=6803222 (Reuters)]{{Dead link|date=August 2021 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}
* Former [[Afghanistan|Afghan]] leader [[Mullah Omar|Mullah Mohammed Omar]] has made a rallying call to his [[Taliban]] forces.  He sent a two-page message to the [[Afghan Islamic Press]] agency to mark the Muslim [[Eid ul Fitr]] festival. [http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/south_asia/4007015.stm (BBC)]
* A fire has badly damaged a [[mosque]] in the south-eastern village of [[Helden]], Netherlands, in the latest of a series of attacks on Dutch Muslim sites. [http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/world/europe/4008781.stm (BBC)]
